title.text: Admin console: own shell, one list pattern, drawn for ~20 players

decisions.text:
Build notes for the console (rows 1–2)

Source of truth: these boards + admin.css. Every colour, face and space is a kit token; light and dark are the same markup under data-theme. No hex.

Data is a ~20-player launch: 1 report, 21 people, 10 tasks. The empty Reports state is the screen mods see most.

Every control is 44px.

Rail is one shared component (Rail.dc.html). Groups: Needs you / Run the game / Words, and Danger fenced at the bottom.

One list pattern: toolbar (search · status segments with counts · chips · one main action) over a table; a row opens a side panel. Ban, suspend and delete live only in panels.

Decided in review (2026-11-19):
• In: empty state, photo in the report, a reason the author sees on Remove and Doesn't-meet-the-task (renamed from Fail), shared mod log (reverses #237's session-only log), 48h proposal countdown, vote ring vs eligible recipients, Small world page, era preflight.
• Out for now: flagger track record (too few flags at launch to mean anything), push-to-one-report (no push yet: #3653, #2164).

Not pictured, same pattern: Praxis, Messages, the copy sheets.

title2.text: Where admin meets the player site: one door, two modes

placement.text:
Placement rules (for whoever builds this)

Hosting: stays at /admin in the same SPA. No admin.worldzero.org: it would need a Caddy block, a second build, a wider COOKIE_DOMAIN and CORS, to isolate ~3 mods. Revisit only for non-player staff.

Shell: /admin/* gets its own layout (rail, no player sidebar). '← Back to World Zero' tops the rail.

One door: the ADMIN nav link goes. The MOD control carries the count badge (reports + messages + proposals) and opens a menu: 'Edit on the page' toggle + 'Open admin'.

Two modes:
• Mod mode = one object, in place, reversible (copy wording, task status, hide a praxis). Page gets an accent frame so it can't be forgotten on.
• Console = queues, search, people, bulk, irreversible (ban, suspend, era).

Same action, same component: the task-status strip on TaskCard and the console panel mount one shared control. Each side links to the other ('Open in admin' / 'View on site').
